description:
Found while wiring rheology into the mechanics solve (op-6sl.11).

MechanicsSolver recovers the stress from fvc::grad_vec(D), which on a 1-D
structured mesh is the wide (2*dx) central-difference gradient. Where the
accumulated inelastic strain is DISCONTINUOUS across a material interface, that
recovery smears the jump over the two cells either side and reports a stress
there that violates 1-D equilibrium.

Measured 2026-08-05 (8-cell bar, cells 0-3 creeping with a linear Norton law,
cells 4-7 purely elastic, 200 steps of tau/20, both x-ends displacement-pinned):
  cell 3: sigma_xx = 18.2785 MPa
  cell 4: sigma_xx = 23.5674 MPa
  cells 5,6,7: sigma_xx = 20.75560 MPa, agreeing to 13 significant figures
i.e. a 25% spread concentrated entirely at the interface, with an exactly
uniform far field.

With a SMOOTHLY varying creep rate the spread converges away under refinement
(whole-bar 3.47e-3 -> 1.64e-3 -> 7.95e-4 at n = 16/32/64, first order because of
the one-sided end cells; interior-only 3.37e-4 -> 1.12e-4 -> 3.44e-5, close to
second order), so the equilibrium the solver ENFORCES is right. It is the stress
RECOVERY that is inaccurate at a discontinuity.

This is the trade-off OpenFOAM exposes as the solidDisplacement
'compactNormalStress' switch: the compact form uses snGrad (more convergent,
less accurate) and the non-compact form uses grad (less convergent, more
accurate). The port currently implements only the grad form for recovery.

Options: (a) port the compactNormalStress switch, including the
divSigmaExp = fvc::div(DEqn.flux()) branch that this port does not have;
(b) recover the stress from face snGrad instead; (c) document that a material
interface needs mesh refinement across it. Today the limitation is documented
and measured on
mechanics::solver::rheology_tests::spatially_varying_creep_keeps_the_axial_stress_uniform.

---
RE-FILED 2026-08-12 with its original id. This bead was created in an earlier session but never published, because beads-rs `bd` could not push the store ref (kopitiam#19). It survived only in the local v1 store, which diverged from origin's migrated v2 store. Preserved at ref refs/beads/local-preserve-20260812. Original status at preservation: open.
title: offbeat mechanics: compact stress recovery for material interfaces (fvc::grad smears a discontinuous inelastic strain)

description:
unresr::mf2::parse_lru2_ranges returns EndfParse('NRO=1 ... not yet ported') for any LRU=2 range with NRO=1. ENDF/B-VIII.0 U-238 (reference-data/endf/n-092_U_238.endf) has exactly that: its URR record is [2.0e4, 1.490087e5, LRU=2, LRF=2, NRO=1, NAPS=0] followed by an 83-point INT=5 TAB1 AP(E). So neither unresolved_cross_sections nor purr::probability_table can run on U-238 today, which is the nuclide op-mzvp.2.12 needs.

Upstream: unresr.f90:517 and purr.f90:806 read the TAB1 with tab1io/moreio into the scratch array right after the range record (before the LSSF/spin CONT); unresl (unresr.f90:966-1001) and unresx (purr.f90:1342-1377) then 'call terpa(ay,e,enx,idx,arry(iro),ip,ir)' to interpolate AP at the working energy and, when NAPS=2, also use it as the channel radius (aaa). The port already has endf::interp::eval_tab1 for the interpolation; the work is (1) parse and store the TAB1 in UnresolvedRange, (2) evaluate it per energy in range_sequences / channel_radius_urr instead of the scalar ap, (3) an oracle test on U-238 with the in-session NJOY build (see op-cjw.6 comments for the deck).

Filed 2026-09-10 while verifying op-cjw.6 on U-235 (NRO=0), where UNRESR now matches NJOY to 4 figures.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
PORTED AND VERIFIED 2026-09-10 (tests/purr_u238_urr.rs, 3 tests). Upstream read first: rdunf2 (unresr.f90:515-528) and rdf2un (purr.f90:804-817) read the TAB1 with tab1io/moreio into arry right after the range CONT; unresl (unresr.f90:966-977, 995-1005) and unresx (purr.f90:1342-1353, 1373-1381) then do ip=2/ir=1 + terpa(ay,e,...) every energy, use ay for rhoc=k*ay (phase shift) and, when NAPS=1, the channel radius, and read aaa=arry(inow+1) (the SPI/AP/LSSF header scalar) as the channel radius only when NAPS=2. terpa (endf.f90:1729-1818): zero below the first node, last value within a 1.00001 shade above the last node, zero beyond.

Port: unresr::mf2::ScatteringRadiusTable {interp, xy} with at(e) reproducing terpa's edge conventions over endf::interp::eval_tab1; Cursor::tab1(); UnresolvedRange.ap_table (Option), UnresolvedRange::scattering_radius(e), UnresolvedCase::ap(); range_sequences now returns Result and evaluates ay once per range, SequenceParams carries ap (=ay), ap_cont (=aaa) and nro; channel_radius_urr(awri,naps,nro,ap,ap_cont) gained the NAPS=2+NRO=1 arm (aa=aaa) and errors 'illegal naps' otherwise, as upstream. purr::infinite_dilution_reference updated to the new signatures.

U-238 (ENDF/B-VIII.0, MAT 9237) data facts: URR 2.0e4-1.490087e5 eV, LRU=2 LRF=2 NRO=1 NAPS=0 LSSF=1, TAB1 83 points INT=5 spanning exactly [EL,EH], AP 0.945408 -> 0.9136041, and the header AP=0.0 - so without the table rhoc=0 and potential scattering vanishes. NLS=3: l=0 J=1/2; l=1 J=1/2,3/2; l=2 J=3/2,5/2 (5 sequences, AMUN=1, AMUX=2 or 1, no fission).

NJOY2016 oracle (in-session build, gfortran 13.3.0) deck: moder 20 -21 / reconr -21 -22 (9237, 0.001) / broadr -21 -22 -23 (9237 1 0 0 0, 0.001, 300.) / unresr -21 -23 -24 (9237 1 6 1, 300., 1e10 1e4 1e3 100 10 1) / purr -21 -24 -25 (9237 1 6 20 32 1, 300., same sigz) / moder -25 26. 70 s wall. Listing: UNRESR 83 energies; PURR 'competition starts at 4.5107E+04 (mt 5, 51, 800)', no heating on pendf.

RESULTS. UNRESR (unresolved_cross_sections, 300 K, [1e10, 1]): 20 keV 14.3609/13.8486/0/0.51237 and 12.9107/12.4713/0/0.43939 vs NJOY 14.36/13.85/0/0.5124 and 12.91/12.47/0/0.4394; 60 keV 12.5366/12.2729/0.26369 & 11.9951/11.7471/0.24801 vs 12.54/12.27/0.2637 & 12.00/11.75/0.2480; 100 keV 11.4664/11.2907/0.17576 & 11.1317/10.9633/0.16846 vs 11.47/11.29/0.1758 & 11.13/10.96/0.1685; 149008.6 eV 10.6249/10.4813/0.14355 & 10.3911/10.2528/0.13832 vs 10.62/10.48/0.1435 & 10.39/10.25/0.1383. Every printed figure reproduced (gate 1.5e-3). PURR unresx (infinite_dilution_reference): 20 keV spot 10.9400 (NJOY 10.940) dbar 2.42763 (2.4276) tot/el/cap 14.36093/13.84857/0.512367 vs MT152 7-figure 14.36093/13.84856/0.5123672; 40 keV spot 10.6087 (10.609) dbar 2.31781 (2.3178) 13.29079/12.91497/0.375818 vs 13.29079/12.91497/0.3758178 (gate 2e-5). PURR MC (probability_table, seed -101, nbin 20, nladr 32, nsamp 10000) at 20 keV: aver 14.3509/13.8394/0/0.51146 vs NJOY 14.352/13.841/0/0.51136, pcsd 1.85/1.87/0/2.99 vs 1.81/1.83/0/2.99; direct-sampling sig0=1: 12.538/12.093/0.44560 vs 12.578/12.133/0.44523; self-shielding ratios 0.8758/0.8759/0.8719 vs 0.8764/0.8766/0.8707 (gates 3% abs, 0.02 ratio). Random streams still not bit-identical (as on U-235).

NEGATIVE/UNVERIFIED: NAPS=2 (aa=aaa) and NAPS=1-with-table arms are ported from the same upstream lines but no evaluation in reference-data/endf/ exercises them. PURR infd totals above the 45.1 keV competition threshold include bkg(1)=sigx (rdf3un's lssf=1 sanity check, purr.f90:1195-1215, rewrites bkg to [tot-el-fis-cap,0,0,0]; unrest adds it at :2378) - the port takes that through probability_table's bkg argument but infinite_dilution_reference has no sigx, so the 7-figure unresx comparison was kept below the threshold; documented in src/purr/README.md.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Landed in ca1b6cae on develop. NRO=1 energy-dependent scattering-radius TAB1 now parsed for LRU=2 ranges and interpolated per energy with terpa conventions; channel_radius_urr gained the NAPS=2-with-NRO=1 arm. U-238's URR (20-149.0087 keV) was unreachable before this: it writes AP=0.0 in its header and carries AP(E) as an 83-point log-log table, so without the table rho_c = 0 and the whole band's potential scattering vanished. Verified against NJOY2016 built in-session (tests/purr_u238_urr.rs): UNRESR reproduces every printed figure at 20/60/100/149.0086 keV for sig0 = 1e10 and 1 b; unresx to 7 figures at 20/40 keV; probability_table means and self-shielding ratios to 3-4 figures.

title: njoy UNRESR/PURR: port NRO=1 (energy-dependent scattering radius) for LRU=2 ranges - blocks U-238 URR
